doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Doin' It Right Now, the Rahsaan-produced album
summary: They discuss the 1972 album and the Atlantic A&R man's pressure.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: You said you didn’t have any records out. But the record that Rahsaan produced, you did that in like ’72 or something like that. Doin’ It.
Well, it was in ’72, but the only thing was, it wasn’t on none of the jukeboxes or nothing.
Oh, it didn’t come out?
No, and there was entirely no publicity.
What was it called? Doin’ it Right Now?
Doin’ it Right Now. That’s the one that they just – that they claim is so great.
Sam Jones is on it.
Yeah, and Jimmy Cobb’s playing drums.
And John Young.
And John Young.
It is good.
They was – it’s supposed to be a classic now.
But it’s different. You’re playing different on that than you were playing on the stuff I started taping.
Oh, of course. Well, you started taping – what? – 20 years later or something like that?
No, no, no. I – the first stuff I have is like ’76, ’77. Before I could play anything, I was taping you and trying to figure out what was happening.

Oh. See, the guy at Atlantic, the A&R man told me, he says, “Now, Freeman, we’re trying to sell records now. We heard that you can – you’re kind of out, outish.” So I say, “Oh, is that what you heard?” He says, “Yeah. We’re still trying to . . .” – and then they didn’t push the records.
Don’t that kill you, though?
Oh yeah.
A cat hires you for what you do, and then here he comes telling you – trying to tell you what to do, and he don’t play himself.
That’s right.
That’s always killed me. I’m like, why didn’t you just get somebody that already does what it is you want? Why are you going to hire an apple and tell him to be an orange?
